question: Who among the following joined the Planning Commission as its Vice-Chairman in March 1950?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulzarilal Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gulzarilal Nanda** joined the **Planning Commission** as its **Vice-Chairman** in **March 1950**.
 
• The Planning Commission was established in **1950** by the Government of India to promote economic development and create systematic plans for growth.
 
• Gulzarilal Nanda was a renowned Indian politician, economist, and administrator known for his contributions to economic planning and labor welfare.
 
• He held key positions in the Indian government, including acting as the **Prime Minister of India** twice in 1964 and 1966.
 
• The Planning Commission aimed at formulating **Five-Year Plans** to guide India's socioeconomic development, and Nanda’s tenure contributed to shaping early strategies for growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• It was established in **1950** under the chairmanship of **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
• The commission was responsible for creating **Five-Year Plans** to boost India’s economic growth and development.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan focused on agricultural development, as agriculture was the backbone of the Indian economy at that time.
 
• Later, the commission worked on industrialization, infrastructure development, and poverty alleviation.
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by **NITI Aayog** in **2015** to reflect modern governance needs.
 
 
 
• **Gulzarilal Nanda:**
 
 
• Born on **4 July 1898** in Sialkot, Punjab (now in Pakistan).
 
• He was known for his expertise in **labor welfare** and economic policies.
 
• He served as the acting Prime Minister of India twice, following the deaths of **Jawaharlal Nehru** in 1964 and **Lal Bahadur Shastri** in 1966.
 
• Nanda was honored with the **Bharat Ratna**, India’s highest civilian award, for his contributions to the nation.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• The first Five-Year Plan (1951–56) aimed at **developing agriculture** and irrigation.
 
• The second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) focused on **industrialization**, particularly heavy industries.
 
• These plans were inspired by the Soviet model of centralized economic planning.
 
• The Planning Commission guided the implementation of these plans to achieve long-term economic goals.
 
 
 
• **Other notable personalities mentioned:**
 
 
• **Jagjivan Ram:** A prominent leader who worked extensively for the upliftment of Dalits and served as Union Minister in various portfolios.
 
• **Shyama Prasad Mukherjee:** Founder of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and a key figure in modern Indian politics.
 
• **John Mathai:** An economist who served as India’s Finance Minister and contributed significantly to the early economic policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Planning Commission Structure:** The commission was headed by the Prime Minister and included a Vice-Chairman, full-time members, and a Secretary.
 
• **Objectives:** The primary aim was to improve living standards through planned economic development and poverty reduction.
 
• **NITI Aayog:** It replaced the Planning Commission to promote decentralized planning and encourage innovation in policymaking.
